To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

time-resolved single-crystalline diffraction performed with a synchrotron X-ray beam shows that a 53 micros phosphorescence, generated in a crystalline matrix by the exposure of trimeric {3,5-(F3)2Pyz]Cu}(3} molecules to 355 nm light, is due to a Cu...Cu intermolecular bond formed by the intermetallic electron transfer from one Cu atom to the other.

the 53 micros phosphorescence observed in the crystalline solid of trimeric Cu(II) complexes is due to the excitation of the trimeric unit to a state that is stabilized by the formation of an intermolecular Cu-Cu bond.
a Cu...Cu excimer is formed in a trimeric {[4,5-(CF 3)2Pyrazolate]2Cu}3 molecule upon photoexcitation at 355 nm, which is the first observation of an excimer formed between two metal centers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the photoinduced formation and structure of a transient excimer, which is the result of a chemical reaction that occurs in the solid phase.
the study of the structure of a transient excimer generated by a photoinduced reaction.
the study of the structure of a transient excimer, formed by the irradiation with UV light of a trinuclear Cu(II) complex, and with the mechanism of the formation of the excimer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 53 ns state is due to the excimer formed by a Cu...Cu interaction between the trimers.
the excimer state of {[3,5-CF3Pyrazolate] Cu}(3) is formed upon excitation of the crystalline material at 17 K by the 355 nm of laser light.
the 53 micros phosphorescence of {[3,5(CF3)(2)Pyrz]Cu}(3), generated in its crystalline phase by exposure to 35 nm of light at low temperature, arises from the formation of a transient excimer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that a Cu...Cu interaction can be induced photochemically, and that the Cu 3d orbital is involved in the interaction.

we have shown that the 3.5 eV excited state is a transient excimer, and that the Cu...Cu bond is formed by the transfer of an electron from a 3d orbital to an orbital of 4p character, which is consistent with the fact that the 4p orbitals are the most diffuse of the d-block orbitals.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the photoinduced formation of the 53(μs) phosphorescence is due to the excimer formation, and not to a shortening of the Cu...Cu intramolecular distances within the trinuclear units, or to the formation of a one-dimensional chain of interacting trimers.
the photoinduced transient state is a molecular excimer, which is a rare example of a transient excimer in the crystalline state.
